<h1>Environment Agency Real Time flood-monitoring API</h1>

<div class="survey-banner" role="region" aria-labelledby="survey-banner-title">
    <div class="survey-banner__header">
      <h2 class="survey-banner__title" id="survey-banner-title">
        Survey
      </h2>
    </div>
    <div class="survey-banner__content">
      <p class="survey-banner__heading">
        Help us to improve this website and API.
        <a class="survey-banner__link" href="https://forms.office.com/Pages/ResponsePage.aspx?id=UCQKdycCYkyQx044U38RAlS_vYS6otFJmqjW5Hudy4hUMkVSSVI2VUlSOTQ4RU9FOVVaTTVBNlowRyQlQCN0PWcu">Complete our short survey</a>.
      </p>
    </div>
  </div>
<span class="anchor" id="introduction"></span>
<h2>Introduction</h2>

<p>The Environment Agency flood-monitoring API provides developers with access to near real time information covering:</p>
<ul>
    <li>flood warnings and flood alerts</li>
    <li>flood areas which to which warnings or alerts apply</li>
    <li>measurements of water levels and flows</li>
    <li>information on the monitoring stations providing those measurements</li>
</ul>

<p>Water levels and flows are regularly monitored, usually every 15 minutes.  However, data is transferred back to the Environment Agency at various frequencies, usually depending on the site and level of flood risk.  Transfer of data is typically once or twice per day, but usually increases during times of heightened flood risk.</p>

<p>These APIs are provided as open data under the <a href="https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/doc/open-government-licence/version/3/" title="This link takes you to a third party site" aria-label="Open Government Licence - This link takes you to a third party site">Open Government Licence</a> with no requirement for registration. If you make use of this data please acknowledge this with the following attribution statement:</p>

<blockquote class="attribution">this uses Environment Agency flood and river level data from the real-time data API (Beta)</blockquote>

<span class="anchor" id="availability"></span>
<h2>Note on crawling</h2>

<p>A common requirement is for an application to maintain a copy of all the latest level/flow values from some (or all) of the measurement stations. The efficient way to do this is to issue a single call every 15 mins:</p>

<p class="indented"><a href="/flood-monitoring/data/readings?latest">https://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/data/readings?latest</a></p>

<p>This will retrieve the latest value for all measurements - from which you can pick the ones you are interested. Since the data changes at most every 15 mins then this single call four times an hour will ensure a complete track of all of the data. </p>
<p>This is <strong>much</strong> preferable to crawling all the stations every 15 mins picking up a single <em>latest</em> value for each station one at a time.</p>

<p>However, this is not sufficient to maintain a complete historical trace since readings are sometimes updated batches. For that purpose a query for the relevant station readings using the <code>since</code> filter is appropriate.</p>

<h2>Availability and resilience</h2>

<p>While they are intended to be stable and robust the open data APIs do not offer a guarantee of service level and should not be relied upon for safety critical applications. They do not replace the <a href="https://www.gov.uk/check-if-youre-at-risk-of-flooding" title="This link takes you to a third party site" aria-label="Check your risk of flooding - This link takes you to a third party site">existing channels</a> by which the Agency notifies members of the public and partner organizations of floods and flood risk.</p>

<p><b>Redirects.</b> At times of high load or in future versions of this API the service may redirect to an alternative URL. Client code should be written so as to follow standard HTTP redirects.</p>

<p><b>Caching.</b> API responses may be cached for a short period within the serving infrastructure or a content delivery network. At times of high load then limiting API use to common patterns (avoiding custom filtering) will improve the chances of cache hits and so good response times. These common patterns are:</p>
<ul>
    <li><span class="linkColour">https://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/id/floods</span></li>
    <li><span class="linkColour">https://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/id/floods?min-severity={x}</span></li>
    <li><span class="linkColour">https://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/id/3dayforecast</span></li>
    <li><span class="linkColour">https://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/id/3dayforecast/image/{day}</span></li>
    <li><span class="linkColour">https://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/data/readings?latest</span></li>
</ul>

<span class="anchor" id="recent"></span>
<h2>Recent updates</h2>

<p>
  <strong>Version 0.8:</strong>
  Added access to Rainfall data.
</p>

<p>
  <strong>Version 0.7:</strong>
</p>
<ul>
    <li>Added fine grain <code>since</code> filter for readings.</li>
    <li>Added <code>_view=full</code> option for listing stations (includes scale information).</li>
    <li>Implemented geo-filter for flood warning areas.</li>
    <li>Added support station status data where available (<code>status</code>, <code>statusReason</code>, <code>statusDate</code>).</li>
    <li>Added support for <code>Last-Modified</code> headers and <code>If-Modified-Since</code> requests</li>
    <li>Added html view options for APIs that return lists of results.</li>
    <li>Improved detection of bad API requests.</li>
    <li>Changes to underlying platform may affect the order of columns in CSV results but not the columns themselves.</li>
</ul>

<p>
  <strong>Version 0.6.1:</strong>
  Enabled filters for station type and status.
</p>

<p>
  <strong>Version 0.6:</strong>
  Added support CSV format out for listing stations.
  Include lat/long and easting/northing in stations listing.
</p>

<span class="anchor" id="api-summary"></span>
<h2>API summary</h2>

<p>This is a brief summary of the APIs available. In the links in the tables <code>{root}</code> corresponds to <code>https://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring</code>.</p>

<h3>Flood warnings</h3>

<table class="table table-condensed table-bordered">
    <thead>
        <tr><th>What</th><th>API</th><th>Parameters</th></tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
        <tr>
            <td>All flood warnings and alerts:</td>
            <td><a href="/flood-monitoring/id/floods">{root}/id/floods</a></td>
            <td><code>min-severity</code>, <code>county</code>, <code>lat=y&amp;long=x&amp;dist=r</code></td>
        </tr>
    </tbody>
</table>

            <td><code>latest</code>, <code>today</code>, <code>date=d</code>, <code>startdate=d1&amp;enddate=d2</code>, <code>since=dt</code>, <code>_view=full</code>, <code>_sorted</code></td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
            <td>All readings for measures from a particular station:</td>
            <td><a href="/flood-monitoring/id/stations/1491TH/readings?_sorted&_limit=100">{root}/id/stations/{id}/readings</a></td>
            <td><code>latest</code>, <code>today</code>, <code>date=d</code>, <code>startdate=d1&amp;enddate=d2</code>, <code>since=dt</code>, <code>_view=full</code>, <code>_sorted</code></td>
        </tr>
    </tbody>

<span class="anchor" id="api-structure"></span>
<h2>API structure</h2>

<p>The APIs provide a <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Representational_state_transfer" title="This link takes you to a third party site" aria-label="About REST APIs - This link takes you to a third party site">REST</a> style access to the data via simple HTTP GET requests which return data in JSON format. Some data is also available in other formats.</p>

<span class="anchor" id="api-requests"></span>
<h3>Simple requests</h3>

<p>For example fetching data from: <a href="/flood-monitoring/id/floods">https://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/id/floods</a></p>

<p>will return a JSON data packet such as:</p>

<pre><code class="json">{
  "@context" : "http://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/doc/context-TBD.jsonld" ,
  "meta" : {
    "publisher": "Environment Agency",
    "licence": "http://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/doc/open-government-licence/version/3/",
    "documentation": "http://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/doc/reference",
    "version": "0.4",
    "comment": "WARNING: Alpha test service, may not be stable",
    "hasFormat": [
        "http://localhost:8080/api/id/floods/91436.rdf",
        "http://localhost:8080/api/id/floods/91436.ttl"
    ]
  },
  "items" : [ {
    "@id" : "http://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/id/floods/91436" ,
    "description" : "North Sea Coast from Whitby to Filey" ,
    "eaAreaName" : "Yorkshire" ,
    "eaRegionName" : "North East" ,
    "floodArea" : { ... } ,
    "floodAreaID" : "122WAC953" ,
    "isTidal" : true ,
    "severity" : "Warning no longer in force" ,
    "severityLevel" : 4 ,
    "timeMessageChanged" : "2015-02-02T19:32:00" ,
    "timeRaised" : "2015-02-02T19:32:00" ,
    "timeSeverityChanged" : "2015-02-02T19:32:00"
  } , ... ]
}</code></pre>

<p>The returned JSON data from all API endpoints follows the same structure of three elements: context, metadata and item(s).</p>

<p>The <code>@context</code> reference is provided to enable the JSON data to be read as <a href="https://json-ld.org/" title="This link takes you to a third party site" aria-label="About json-ld - This link takes you to a third party site">json-ld</a>.</p>

<span class="anchor" id="api-metadata"></span>
<h3>Metadata and versioning</h3>

<p>The metadata block:</p>

<pre><code class="json">"meta" : {
    "publisher": "Environment Agency",
    "licence": "http://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/doc/open-government-licence/version/3/",
    "documentation": "http://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/doc/reference",
    "version": "0.4",
    "comment": "WARNING: Alpha test service, may not be stable",
    "hasFormat": [
        "http://localhost:8080/api/id/floods/91436.rdf",
        "http://localhost:8080/api/id/floods/91436.ttl"
    ]
  }</code></pre>

<p>provides information on the publisher and applicable licence as well as a link to this, or other, documentation. If the resource is also available in other formats then <code>hasFormat</code> will supply list of URLs for those alternative formats (the media type is implied a suffix, see <a href="#api-content-types">content types</a>).</p>

<p>The metadata block also includes version number information. The intention is that updates to the API should maintain backward compatibility. If an incompatible change to the API is required then we will attempt to provide access to the prior version for a transitional period. In that case the <code>meta</code> block will also provide <code>replaces</code> and <code>isReplacedBy</code> links between the new and the old versions of the affected API endpoints. </p>

<p>Finally, in the case of calls which provide lists of results then any applied limit to the length of the list and offset from the start of the list will be shown in the metadata as <code>limit</code> and <code>offset</code> values, for example:</p>
<pre><code class="json">"meta" : {
    "publisher" : "Environment Agency" ,
    "licence" : "http://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/doc/open-government-licence/version/3/" ,
    "documentation" : "http://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/doc/reference" ,
    "version" : "0.4" ,
    "comment" : "WARNING: Alpha test service, may not be stable" ,
    "limit" : 10,
    "offset" : 5
  }</code></pre>

<p>Note that some endpoints impose a length limit even if one has not be specified explicitly by the caller. The metadata is particularly useful in this case as a warning that this has occurred.</p>

<span class="anchor" id="api-items"></span>
<h3>Items</h3>
<p>The <code>items</code> element in the JSON response will contain either a description of a single item or an array of items. For API endpoints which return lists of items (e.g. all measurement stations of a certain kind) then value will always be an array even if the list only has one entry. For API endpoints which describe a specific item (e.g. a particular measurement station) the value will always be an object, with no wrapping array.</p>

<p>Each item will normally be identified by a URI given in the <code>@id</code> field. Thus, for example in the fuller version of the earlier example:</p>
<pre><code class="json"> "items" : [ {
    "@id" : "http://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/id/floods/91436" ,
    "description" : "North Sea Coast from Whitby to Filey" ,
    "eaAreaName" : "Yorkshire" ,
    "eaRegionName" : "North East" ,
    "floodArea" : {
      "@id" : "http://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/id/floodAreas/122WAC953" ,
      "county" : "North Yorkshire" ,
      "notation" : "122WAC953" ,
      "polygon" : "http://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/id/floodAreas/122WAC953/polygon" ,
      "riverOrSea" : "North Sea"
    }
     ,
    "floodAreaID" : "122WAC953" ,
    "isTidal" : true ,
    "severity" : "Warning no longer in force" ,
    "severityLevel" : 4 ,
    "timeMessageChanged" : "2015-02-02T19:32:00" ,
    "timeRaised" : "2015-02-02T19:32:00" ,
    "timeSeverityChanged" : "2015-02-02T19:32:00"
  } ... ] </code></pre>

<p>we can see the flood warning itself has an identifier (note that warnings have a limited lifetime so this URL isn't live any more):</p>
<div class="indented"><span class="linkColour">https://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/id/floods/91436</span></div>
<p>as does the flood area to which the warning applies:</p>
<div class="indented"><a href="/flood-monitoring/id/floodAreas/122WAC953">https://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/id/floodAreas/122WAC953</a></div>

<p>When one item references another, such as in this case, the API will typically include key attributes of the referenced item in-line for convenience. However, we can always fetch (GET) data from the reference item URI to obtain a full description. For example, dereferencing the flood area URI returns:</p>
<pre><code class="json">  {
    "@id" : "http://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/id/floodAreas/122WAC953" ,
    "county" : "North Yorkshire" ,
    "currentWarning" : { ... } ,
    "description" : "The North Sea coast from Whitby to Filey, including Scarborough" ,
    "eaAreaName" : "Yorkshire" ,
    "eaRegionName" : "North East Region" ,
    "fwdCode" : "122WAC953" ,
    "label" : "North Sea Coast from Whitby to Filey" ,
    "notation" : "122WAC953" ,
    "polygon" : "http://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/id/floodAreas/122WAC953/polygon" ,
    "quickDialNumber" : "130401" ,
    "riverOrSea" : "North Sea" ,
    "type" : [ "http://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/def/core/FloodAlertArea", "http://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/def/core/FloodArea" ]
  }</code></pre>

<p>Many of these URIs are stable long term reference identifiers e.g. the flood areas, the measurement stations and the individual measurement types are stable. However, some items may only be transient. For example, the URI for an individual flood alert may only remain valid for a few days. The severity of the alert, and associated message, may change over that time eventually reducing to severity level 4 (<em>Warning no longer in force</em>). After that the alert will disappear and that URI will no longer resolve, returning a 404.</p>

<span class="anchor"  id="api-content-types"></span>
<h3>Content Types</h3>
<p>The descriptions of individual items can be obtained in multiple formats. The default format is JSON but all item descriptions can also return information in RDF formats (RDF/XML and Turtle). In addition some items offer a simple HTML rendering which makes it possible to look at these reference identifiers conveniently in a browser. The HTML rendering is intended as an aid to help developers understand the data, it is not an end-user application.</p>

<p>Similarly lists of items can be obtained in multiple formats. The default is JSON (in which the <code>items</code> field will contain an array of objects) but they are also typically also available in CSV format.</p>

<p>To select the desired format use standard HTTP content negation. E.g.:</p>
<pre><code class="bash"> curl -i -H "Accept: text/turtle" https://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/id/floodAreas/122WAC953</code></pre>

<p>All endpoints also support a short cut of appending a type suffix to the URI to force a particular content type. The supported suffixes are:</p>
<table class="table table-condensed table-bordered">
    <thead>
        <tr><th>Suffix</th><th>Type</th></tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
        <tr><td>.json</td><td>application/json</td></tr>
        <tr><td>.ttl</td><td>text/turtle</td></tr>
        <tr><td>.rdf</td><td>application/rdf+xml</td></tr>
        <tr><td>.html</td><td>text/html</td></tr>
        <tr><td>.csv</td><td>text/csv</td></tr>
    </tbody>
</table>

<span class="anchor"  id="api-lists"></span>
<h3>Lists: filtering and paging</h3>

<p>Some endpoints return information describing a single identified item but many return information on a list of items. In that case the value of the <code>items</code> field is an array of items. Such list endpoints support query parameters to filter the list to only include some items, for example:</p>

<div class="indented"><a href="/flood-monitoring/id/floods?min-severity=3">https://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/id/floods?min-severity=3</a></div>

<p>returns a list of all flood alerts and warnings which are of severity 3 of worse.</p>

<p>The specific filters available depend on the endpoint and are documented in the following tables. Though many endpoints will support two common filters:</p>

    <table class="table table-condensed table-bordered">
        <thead>
            <tr><th>Query</th><th>Meaning</th></tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
            <tr><td><code class="nowrap">?search=x</code></td><td>Return only those items whose label contains <code>x</code></td></tr>
            <tr><td><code class="nowrap">?lat=y&amp;long=x&amp;dist=d</code></td><td>return those items whose location falls within <code>d</code> km of the given latitude/longitude (in WGS84 coordinates), this may be approximated by a bounding box. </td></tr>
        </tbody>
    </table>

<p>In addition to filtering then list endpoints support view modification parameters, these are distinguished by starting with an underscore character. The commonly supported modifiers are:</p>

    <table class="table table-condensed table-bordered">
        <thead>
            <tr><th>Query</th><th>Meaning</th></tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
            <tr><td><code class="nowrap">?_view=full</code></td><td>Return a full description of each item in the list, instead of the default minimal description. Only relevant for some endpoints.</td></tr>
            <tr><td><code class="nowrap">?_limit=x</code></td><td>Return only <code>x</code> items from the list, some endpoints may impose a default limit and/or a maximum to which the limit can be set.</td></tr>
            <tr><td><code class="nowrap">?_offset=x</code></td><td>Return the list of items starting with the <code>x</code>th item, together with <code>_limit</code> this enables paging through a long set of reults.</td></tr>
        </tbody>
    </table>

<p>If a limit or offset is applicable, whether explicit in the query or implicitly imposed by the API, then the metadata object will include a <code>limit</code> or <code>offset</code> field to show what limits were applied.</p>

<span class="anchor" id="flood-warnings"></span>
<h2>Flood warnings</h2>

<p>The Environment Agency issue warnings of floods that cover specific warning or alert areas. The floods API provides a listing of all current such warnings and is updated every 15 minutes.</p>

<p>A warning may be at one of four possible severity levels:</p>

    <table class="table table-condensed table-bordered">
        <thead>
            <tr><th>Level</th><th>Name</th><th>Meaning</th></tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
            <tr><td>1</td><td>Severe Flood Warning</td><td>Severe Flooding, Danger to Life.</td></tr>
            <tr><td>2</td><td>Flood Warning</td><td>Flooding is Expected, Immediate Action Required.</td></tr>
            <tr><td>3</td><td>Flood Alert</td><td>Flooding is Possible, Be Prepared.</td></tr>
            <tr><td>4</td><td>Warning no Longer in Force</td><td>The warning is no longer in force</td></tr>
        </tbody>
    </table>

<h3>API</h3>
<p><strong>An update to the Flood Warning API took place on 30 June 2020</strong>. Although as much as possible has been done to ensure limited knock on effects to end users, please contact us via the feedback links to report any issue.  The main change is in the way the <code>@id</code> and URI of the individual flood warning is constructed. </p>
<p>The list of current flood warnings:</p>
<div class="indented"><a href="/flood-monitoring/id/floods">https://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/id/floods</a></div>

<p>Supports the following filter parameter:</p>
   <table class="table table-condensed table-bordered">
        <thead>
            <tr><th>Query</th><th>Meaning</th></tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
            <tr><td><code class="nowrap">?min-severity=x</code></td><td>Return only warnings which at least as severe as level <code>x</code></td></tr>
            <tr><td><code class="nowrap">?county=x</code></td><td>Return only warnings applying to flood areas whose county name contains the string <code>x</code>. <code>x</code> can be a list of county names separated by "," in which case alerts which mention any of the named counties will be returned.</td></tr>
            <tr><td><code class="nowrap">?lat=y&long=x&dist=r</code></td><td>Return only warnings applying to flood areas which are within <code>r</code>km of the given latitude/longitude (in WGS84 coordinates), this may be approximated by a bounding box.</td></tr>
        </tbody>
    </table>

<p>So for example, to find all warnings that are currently in effect use:</p>
<div class="indented"><a href="/flood-monitoring/id/floods?min-severity=3">https://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/id/floods?min-severity=3</a></div>

<p>To find all warnings that apply to areas in Somerset use:</p>
<div class="indented"><a href="/flood-monitoring/id/floods?county=Somerset">https://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/id/floods?county=Somerset</a></div>

<p>Each individual warning with have a URI given by the <code>@id</code> field in the data:</p>
<div class="indented"><span class="linkColour">https://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/id/floods/{id}</span></div>

<p>The <code>{id}</code> section of this URI is taken from the value of the <code>floodAreaID</code>.  Therefore the current warning for a flood area (if any warning exists) will always have the same URI.</p>

<p>The severity level and the message field may change through the lifetime of the warning. The data for a warning will include the time at which the severity last changed. At some point after a warning is no longer in force it will disappear from the data feed and the URI for that warning will cease to resolve. If no warning is currently in place for that flood area, then attempting to resolve the URI will return a 404 status code.</p>

<p>For approximately 24 hours after a warning has been in place for a flood area, the severity level will be set to 4, "Warning no Longer in Force", before the warning response is removed altogether.</p>

<h3>Returned data</h3>
<table class='table table-condensed table-bordered'>
  <thead>
    <tr><th>Field</th><th>Meaning</th><th>Type</th><th>Occurs</th></tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td><code>description</code></td><td>Descriptive name for the flood area affected</td><td>xsd:string</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>eaAreaName</code></td><td>Name of the relevant Environment Agency Area</td><td>xsd:string</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>eaRegionName</code></td><td>No longer used</td><td>xsd:string</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>floodArea</code></td><td>URI for the flood alert or flood warning area affected</td><td></td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>floodAreaID</code></td><td>Internal identifier for the flood alert or flood warning area affected</td><td>xsd:string</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>isTidal</code></td><td>True if the flood is tidal, false if not (fluvial or Groundwater)</td><td>xsd:boolean</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>message</code></td><td>The current situation message, also known as the real time commentary</td><td>xsd:string</td><td>optional</td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>severity</code></td><td>The severity of the warning as a text label: 'Flood Alert', 'Flood Warning', 'Severe Flood Warning' or 'Warning no Longer in Force'</td><td>xsd:string</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>severityLevel</code></td><td>Severity level code:  1 = 'Severe Flood Warning', 2 = 'Flood Warning', 3 = 'Flood Alert', 4 = 'Warning no Longer in Force'</td><td>xsd:int</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>timeMessageChanged</code></td><td>The date and time when the message was last changed</td><td>xsd:dateTime</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>timeRaised</code></td><td>The date and time the warning was last reviewed.  Usually (but not always) this leads to a change in the message or severity</td><td>xsd:dateTime</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>timeSeverityChanged</code></td><td>The date and time when the severity level was last changed</td><td>xsd:dateTime</td><td></td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
<p>Structure of nested field <code>floodArea</code>:</p><table class='table table-condensed table-bordered'>
  <thead>
    <tr><th>Field</th><th>Meaning</th><th>Type</th><th>Occurs</th></tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td><code>county</code></td><td>The name of the county intersecting the flood area, as entered by the Flood Incident Management Team</td><td>xsd:string</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>notation</code></td><td>Unique identifier code for the flood area affected</td><td>xsd:string</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>polygon</code></td><td>The boundary of the area encoded as a geoJSON polygon</td><td>xsd:anyURI</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>riverOrSea</code></td><td>Name of the river or sea area linked to the flood area</td><td>xsd:string</td><td>optional</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

<span class="anchor" id="flood-areas"></span>
<h2>Flood areas</h2>

<p>The flood areas API provide information on the geographic regions to which a given flood alert or warning may apply. These comprise <em>Flood Alert Areas</em> and <em>Flood Warning Areas</em>. A Flood Alert Area is a geographical area where it is possible for flooding to occur from rivers, sea and in some locations, groundwater. A single Flood Alert Area may cover a large portion of the floodplain, may contain multiple river catchments of similar characteristics and may contain a number of Flood Warning Areas. A Flood Warning Area is a geographical area where Environment Agency expect flooding to occur and which they provide a Flood Warning Service.</p>

<p>Full information on the areas is available from the Environment Agency <a href="https://environment.data.gov.uk/ds/catalogue/index.jsp#/catalogue">Spatial Data Catalogue</a> as a downloadable file and via a Web Feature Service or Web Mapping Service. For convenience we here provide the feature information for each area as a simple JSON format, including a specification of the polygon for each area (as a geoJSON feature in WGS84 coordinates). A typical application should maintain a local copy of the geographic information rather that reply on on-demand downloads of the rather large polygon files.</p>

<p>Each flood warning provides a link (<code>floodArea</code>) to the URI of the flood area to which it applies.</p>

<h3>API</h3>

<p>To describe an individual area</p>
<div class="indented"><a href="/flood-monitoring/id/floodAreas/122WAC953">https://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/id/floodAreas/{area-code}</a></div>

<p>To list all flood areas (several thousand):</p>
<div class="indented"><a href="/flood-monitoring/id/floodAreas">https://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/id/floodAreas</a></div>

<p>Supports the following filter parameter:</p>
   <table class="table table-condensed table-bordered">
        <thead>
            <tr><th>Query</th><th>Meaning</th></tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
            <tr><td><code class="nowrap">?lat=y&amp;long=x&amp;dist=d</code></td><td>return those areas whose location falls within <code>d</code> km of the given latitude/longitude (in WGS84 coordinates), this may be approximated by a bounding box. </td></tr>
        </tbody>
    </table>

<p>The default limit on number of returned items is 500, this can be adjusted by given an explicit <code>_limit</code> value, there is no hard upper limit.</p>

<h3>Returned data</h3>
<table class='table table-condensed table-bordered'>
  <thead>
    <tr><th>Field</th><th>Meaning</th><th>Type</th><th>Occurs</th></tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td><code>county</code></td><td>The name of the county intersecting the flood area, as entered by the Flood Incident Management Team</td><td></td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>description</code></td><td>A textual description of the item</td><td>xsd:string</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>eaAreaName</code></td><td>Name of the relevant Environment Agency Area</td><td>xsd:string</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>eaRegionName</code></td><td>Name of the relevant Environment Agency region</td><td>xsd:string</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>floodWatchArea</code></td><td>The Flood Watch Area corresponding ot a warning</td><td></td><td>optional</td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>fwdCode</code></td><td>Identifying code for the corresponding Target Area in Flood Warnings direct</td><td>xsd:string</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>label</code></td><td>A name for the item</td><td>xsd:string</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>lat</code></td><td>latitude of the centroid of the area, in WGS84 coordinate ref</td><td>xsd:decimal</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>long</code></td><td>longitude of the centroid of the area, in WGS84 coordinate ref</td><td>xsd:decimal</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>notation</code></td><td>A string or other literal which uniquely identifies the item.</td><td>xsd:string</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>polygon</code></td><td>The boundary of the area encoded as a geoJSON polygon</td><td>xsd:anyURI</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>quickDialNumber</code></td><td>The QuickDial number of flood line for an English language recording</td><td>xsd:string</td><td>optional</td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>riverOrSea</code></td><td>Name of the river or sea area linked to the flood area</td><td>xsd:string</td><td>optional</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

<span class="anchor" id="stations"></span>
<h2>Stations</h2>

<p>The real-time data API provides information on readings of water levels and flows taken at a variety of measurement stations. A given station may provide more than one set of measurements, for example, both water level and flow rate or water level at two different spots (e.g. up-stream and down-stream of a sluice or weir). The API provides metadata on these <em>stations</em> and on the different <em>measures</em> available from each one, as well as the <em>readings</em> themselves.</p>

<h3>API</h3>

<p>To return the list of all measurement stations (several thousand), or some subset thereof:</p>
<div class="indented"><a href="/flood-monitoring/id/stations?_limit=50">https://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/id/stations</a></div>

<p>Supports the following filter parameters:</p>
   <table class="table table-condensed table-bordered">
        <thead>
            <tr><th>Query</th><th>Meaning</th></tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
            <tr><td><code class="nowrap">?parameterName=x</code></td><td>Return only those stations which measure parameters with the given name <code>x</code>, for example <em>Water Level</em> or <em>Flow</em>.</td></tr>
            <tr><td><code class="nowrap">?parameter=x</code></td><td>Return only those stations which measure parameters with the given short form name <code>x</code>, for example <em>level</em> or <em>flow</em>.</td></tr>
            <tr><td><code class="nowrap">?qualifier=x</code></td><td>Return only those stations which measure parameters with qualifier <code>x</code>. Useful qualifiers are <em>Stage</em> and <em>Downstream Stage</em> (for stations such as weirs which measure levels at two locations), <em>Groundwater</em> for groundwater levels as opposed to river levels and <em>Tidal Level</em> for tidal levels.</td></tr>
            <tr><td><code class="nowrap">?label=x</code></td><td>Return only those stations whose <code>label</code> is exactly <code>x</code>.</td></tr>
            <tr><td><code class="nowrap">?town=x</code></td><td>Return only those stations whose <code>town</code> is <code>x</code>. Not all stations have an associated town.</td></tr>
            <tr><td><code class="nowrap">?catchmentName=x</code></td><td>Return only those stations whose catchment name is exactly <code>x</code>. Not all stations have an associated catchment area.</td></tr>
            <tr><td><code class="nowrap">?riverName=x</code></td><td>Return only those stations whose river name is exactly <code>x</code>. Not all stations have an associated river name.</td></tr>
            <tr><td><code class="nowrap">?stationReference=x</code></td><td>Return only those stations whose reference identifier is <code>x</code>. The station reference is an internal identifier used by the Environment Agency.</td></tr>
            <tr><td><code class="nowwrap">?RLOIid=r</code></td><td>Return only the station (if there is one) whose RLOIid (River Levels on the Internet identifier) matches <code>r</code>.</td></tr>
            <tr><td><code class="nowrap">?search=x</code></td><td>Return only those stations whose label contains <code>x</code></td></tr>
            <tr><td><code class="nowrap">?lat=y&amp;long=x&amp;dist=d</code></td><td>return those stations whose location falls within <code>d</code> km of the given latitude/longitude (in WGS84 coordinates), this may be approximated by a bounding box.</td></tr>
            <tr><td><code class="nowrap">?type=x</code></td><td>Return only those stations of the given type, where <code>x</code> can be one of <code>SingleLevel</code>, <code>MultiTraceLevel</code>, <code>Coastal</code>, <code>Groundwater</code> or <code>Meteorological</code></td></tr>
            <tr><td><code class="nowrap">?status=x</code></td><td>Return only those stations with the given status, where <code>x</code> can be one of <code>Active</code>, <code>Closed</code> or <code>Suspended</code></td></tr>
        </tbody>
    </table>

<h3>Examples</h3>

<p>List all stations which measure flow rates:</p>
<div class="indented"><a href="/flood-monitoring/id/stations?parameter=flow">https://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/id/stations?parameter=flow</a></div>

<p>List all stations which measure a downstream level:</p>
<div class="indented"><a href="/flood-monitoring/id/stations?qualifier=Downstream+Stage">https://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/id/stations?qualifier=Downstream+Stage</a></div>

<p>List 10 stations in the Costwold catchment:</p>
<div class="indented"><a href="/flood-monitoring/id/stations?catchmentName=Cotswolds&_limit=10">https://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/id/stations?catchmentName=Cotswolds&amp;_limit=10</a></div>

<p>List all stations whose name includes "River Wey":</p>
<div class="indented"><a href="/flood-monitoring/id/stations?search=River+Wey">https://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/id/stations?search=River+Wey</a></div>

<p>List all stations whose "River name" value is "Cherwell":</p>
<div class="indented"><a href="/flood-monitoring/id/stations?riverName=Cherwell">https://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/id/stations?riverName=Cherwell</a></div>

<h3>Returned data</h3>
<table class='table table-condensed table-bordered'>
  <thead>
    <tr><th>Field</th><th>Meaning</th><th>Type</th><th>Occurs</th></tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td><code>RLOIid</code></td><td>Identifier for the station, as used by River Levels On the Internet.</td><td>xsd:string</td><td>optional</td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>catchmentName</code></td><td>The name of the river catchment which this site is related to, if any</td><td>string</td><td>optional</td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>dateOpened</code></td><td>The date on which the station opened</td><td>xsd:date</td><td>optional</td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>datumOffset</code></td><td>Offset between the reference point for how the data is originally recorded and how it is normally displayed. Normally this is the difference between Ordnance datum and the stage datum</td><td>xsd:decimal</td><td>optional</td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>downstageScale</code></td><td>Scale limits and historic range for the downstream stage water level measure</td><td></td><td>optional</td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>label</code></td><td>A name for the item</td><td>string</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>measures</code></td><td>The set of measurement types available from the station</td><td>rt:Measure</td><td>multi-valued</td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>notation</code></td><td>A string or other literal which uniquely identifies the item.</td><td>xsd:string</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>riverName</code></td><td>Name of river associated with this monitoring station (when available)</td><td>xsd:string</td><td>optional</td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>stageScale</code></td><td>Scale limits and historic range for the main stage water level measure</td><td></td><td>optional</td></tr>

    <tr><td><code>town</code></td><td>Name of the nearest town (or named place) to the station</td><td>string</td><td>optional</td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>wiskiID</code></td><td>Identifier for the station in the WISKI hydrology dataset</td><td>xsd:string</td><td>optional</td></tr>
    <tr>
        <td><code>lat</code></td>
        <td>Latitude of the station, in WGS84 coordinate ref</td>
        <td>xsd:decimal</td><td>optional</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td><code>long</code></td>
        <td>Longitude of the station, in WGS84 coordinate ref</td>
        <td>xsd:decimal</td><td>optional</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td><code>easting</code></td>
        <td>Easting of the station on British National Grid</td>
        <td>xsd:integer</td><td>optional</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td><code>northing</code></td>
        <td>Northing of the station on British National Grid</td>
        <td>xsd:integer</td><td>optional</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td><code>status</code></td>
        <td>The status of the station, one of <code>rt:statusActive</code>, <code>rt:statusClosed</code> or <code>rt:statusSuspended</code></td>
        <td>skos:Concept</td><td>optional</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td><code>statusReason</code></td>
        <td>Provides some explanation of the status or change in status of the station</td>
        <td>xsd:string</td><td>optional</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td><code>statusDate</code></td>
        <td>The date/time of the last update to the status of this station</td>
        <td>xsd:dateTime</td><td>optional</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td><code>type</code></td>
        <td>A list of types for the station, will be <code>rt:Station</code> plus one of <code>rt:SingleLevel</code>, <code>rt:MultiTraceLevel</code>, <code>rt:Coastal</code>, <code>rt:Groundwater</code> or <code>rt:Meteorological</code>.</td>
        <td>owl:Class</td><td></td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
<p>Structure of nested field <code>measures</code>:</p><table class='table table-condensed table-bordered'>
  <thead>
    <tr><th>Field</th><th>Meaning</th><th>Type</th><th>Occurs</th></tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td><code>parameter</code></td><td>Short, canonical, name of the quantity being measured e.g. "level", "flow" or "temperature".</td><td>string</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>parameterName</code></td><td>The name of the quantity being measured e.g. "Water Level", "Flow", "Temperature"</td><td>string</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>period</code></td><td>The period between successive readings, in seconds.</td><td>xsd:decimal</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>qualifier</code></td><td>A qualifier for the quantity being measured. Most common use is to separate level measures which occur at the top ("Stage") or bottom ("Downstream Stage") of a sluice or weir. Other relevant qualifiers are "Tidal Level" and "Groundwater".</td><td>string</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>unitName</code></td><td>A  name for the units for this measurement including the datumType. Typical values are mAOD (for metres relative to the Ordnance Survey datum), mASD (for metres relative to the local stage datum), m (for metres with an unspecified datum) and m3/s (for flow rates).</td><td>xsd:string</td><td></td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

<h3>Views</h3>

<p>In addition to the default view, it is possible to obtain a more complete description of each station in the (filtered) list of stations by using <code>_view=full</code>. This will force the including of stage and downstage scale information (see next sections) when available.</p>

<span class="anchor" id="individual-station"></span>
<h3>API for individual stations</h3>

<p>Given a URI for an individual station then dereferencing it will return a full description of the station. For convenience the station description is available as a rendered HTML page as well as in JSON and RDF format. For example:</p>
<div class="indented"><a href="/flood-monitoring/id/stations/1491TH.html">https://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/id/stations/1491TH.html</a></div>

<p>By default, with no <code>.html</code> suffix you will get data in JSON format though you can also force this using:<p>
<div class="indented"><a href="/flood-monitoring/id/stations/1491TH.json">https://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/id/stations/1491TH.json</a></div>

<p>Or when scripting you can use content negotiation to request a response of media type <code>application/json</code>.</p>

<p>The information returned for an individual station is enriched by also including scale information for those stations for which this is available.</p>
<table class='table table-condensed table-bordered'>
  <thead>
    <tr><th>Field</th><th>Meaning</th><th>Type</th><th>Occurs</th></tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td><code>stageScale</code></td><td>Scale information for the main stage water level measurement.</td><td>rt:Scale</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>downstageScale</code></td><td>Scale information for the downstream water level measurement, if available.</td><td>rt:Scale</td><td></td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

<p>In each case the scale information is an object with the following fields:</p>
<table class='table table-condensed table-bordered'>
  <thead>
    <tr><th>Field</th><th>Meaning</th><th>Type</th><th>Occurs</th></tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td><code>highestRecent</code></td><td>The highest reading for this measurement in recent times (typically the last 5 years)</td><td>rt:Reading</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>maxOnRecord</code></td><td>The highest reading for this measurement on record</td><td>rt:Reading</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>minOnRecord</code></td><td>The lowest reading for this measurement on record</td><td>rt:Reading</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>scaleMax</code></td><td>The maximum of the scale suitable for displaying this measurement.</td><td>xsd:decimal</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>typicalRangeHigh</code></td><td>The top of the typical range band - the measurement exceeded this for 5% of the relevant data on record</td><td>xsd:decimal</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>typicalRangeLow</code></td><td>The bottom of the typical range band - the measurement exceeded this for 95% of the relevant data on record</td><td>xsd:decimal</td><td></td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

<span class="anchor" id="measures"></span>
<h2>Measures</h2>

<p>In additional to listing stations, which includes the information on the measures available from each station, you can list the available measures directly:</p>
<div class="indented"><a href="/flood-monitoring/id/measures?_limit=50">https://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/id/measures</a></div>

<p>Supports the following filter parameters:</p>
   <table class="table table-condensed table-bordered">
        <thead>
            <tr><th>Query</th><th>Meaning</th></tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
            <tr><td><code class="nowrap">?parameterName=x</code></td><td>Return only measures for parameters with the given name <code>x</code>, for example <em>Water Level</em> or <em>Flow</em>.</td></tr>
            <tr><td><code class="nowrap">?parameter=x</code></td><td>Return only measures for parameters with the given short form name <code>x</code>, for example <em>level</em> or <em>flow</em>.</td></tr>
            <tr><td><code class="nowrap">?qualifier=x</code></td><td>Return only those measures with qualifier <code>x</code>. Useful qualifiers are <em>Stage</em> and <em>Downstream Stage</em> (for stations such as weirs which measure levels at two locations), <em>Groundwater</em> for groundwater levels as opposed to river levels and <em>Tidal Level</em> for tidal levels.</td></tr>
            <tr><td><code class="nowrap">?stationReference=x</code></td><td>Return only those measures which are available from the station with the reference identifier <code>x</code>.</td></tr>
            <tr><td><code class="nowrap">?station=x</code></td><td>Return only those measures which are available from the station with the URI <code>x</code>.</td></tr>
        </tbody>
    </table>

<p>For convenience the measures available from a station may also be listed using the URI pattern:</p>
<div class="indented"><a href="/flood-monitoring/id/stations/1491TH/measures">https://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/id/stations/{id}/measures</a></div>

<p>The list of currently available types of measurement are:</p>
   <table class="table table-condensed table-bordered">
        <thead>
            <tr>
                <th>parameterName</th>
                <th>parameter (short name)</th>
                <th>Comments</th>
            </tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
            <tr>
                <td><code>Water Level</code></td>
                <td><code>level</code></td>
                <td>Water level, see qualifier for whether stage or downstream of the stage, see unitName for whether relative to the stage datum (mASD) or to the ordnance datum.</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td><code>Flow</code></td>
                <td><code>flow</code></td>
                <td>Water flow rate, only available from some stations. The units of measurement vary between stations so check the unitName carefully.</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td><code>Wind</code></td>
                <td><code>wind</code></td>
                <td>Wind direction and speed available from some stations. The qualifier will indicate whether direction (degrees) or speed (knots or m/s).</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td><code>Temperature</code></td>
                <td><code>temperature</code></td>
                <td>Dry bulb air temperature measurement available from some stations.</td>
            </tr>
        </tbody>
    </table>

<span class="anchor" id="measure-results"></span>
<h3>Returned data</h3>
<table class='table table-condensed table-bordered'>
  <thead>
    <tr><th>Field</th><th>Meaning</th><th>Type</th><th>Occurs</th></tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td><code>datumType</code></td><td>For level measurements this indicates the type of reference point the level is measured from. Can be relative to the Ordnance Survey datum (rt:AOD), to a local stage datum (rt:ASD) or rt:BDAT (below datum?).</td><td></td><td>optional</td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>label</code></td><td>A name for the item</td><td>xsd:string</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>latestReading</code></td><td>links from a measure the latest available reading</td><td>rt:Reading</td><td>optional</td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>notation</code></td><td>A string or other literal which uniquely identifies the item.</td><td>xsd:string</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>parameter</code></td><td>Short, cannonical, name of the quantity being measured e.g. "level", "flow" or "temperature".</td><td>string</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>parameterName</code></td><td>The name of the quantity being measured e.g. "Water Level", "Flow", "Temperature"</td><td>string</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>period</code></td><td>The period between successive readings, in seconds.</td><td>xsd:decimal</td><td>optional</td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>qualifier</code></td><td>A qualilfier for the quantity being measured. Most common use is to separate level measures which occur at the top ("Stage") or bottom ("Downstream Stage") of a sluice or weir. Other relevant qualifiers are "Tidal Level" and "Groundwater".</td><td>string</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>station</code></td><td>The URI of the monitoring station supplying the measure</td><td>rdfs:Resource</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>stationReference</code></td><td>Identifier for the telemetry feed used by the Environment Agency's National Flood Forecasting System</td><td>string</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>unit</code></td><td>The units in which this parameter is measured, e.g. qudt:Meter</td><td></td><td>optional</td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>unitName</code></td><td>A  name for the units for this measurement including the datumType. Typical values are mAOD (for metres relative to the Ordnance Survey datum), mASD (for metres relative to the local stage datum), m (for metres with an unspecified datum) and m3/s (for flow rates).</td><td>xsd:string</td><td>optional</td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>valueType</code></td><td>Indicates whether the measured value is an instantaneous reading or a total, mean or maximum over the period.</td><td></td><td>optional</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
<p>Structure of nested field <code>latestReading</code>:</p><table class='table table-condensed table-bordered'>
  <thead>
    <tr><th>Field</th><th>Meaning</th><th>Type</th><th>Occurs</th></tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td><code>date</code></td><td>The date at which the reading occurred</td><td>xsd:date</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>dateTime</code></td><td>The date time at which the reading occurred</td><td>xsd:dateTime</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>measure</code></td><td>The URI of the measure being recorded in this reading, this define the location (station), the parameter being measured and other qualifying information.</td><td>rt:Measure</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>value</code></td><td>The value of the reading for the associated measurement, a double not a decimal since some values are NaN. Note that in JSON output NaN is illegal for a number so in JSON any NaN readings will omit the rt:value.</td><td>xsd:double</td><td></td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

<span class="anchor" id="individual-measure"></span>
<h3>API for individual measures</h3>

<p>Given a URI for an individual measure then dereferencing it will return a full description of the measure. For convenience the measure description is available as a rendered HTML page as well as in JSON and RDF format. For example:</p>
<div class="indented"><a href="/flood-monitoring/id/measures/1491TH-level-stage-i-15_min-mASD">https://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/id/measures/1491TH-level-stage-i-15_min-mASD</a></div>

<p>To get the JSON description of the individual use a <code>.json</code> suffix or content negotiation as usual.<p>

<p>The format of an individual measure description is just the same as that for the <a href="#measure-results">measure lists</a>.</p>

<span class="anchor" id="readings"></span>
<h2>Readings</h2>

<p>Readings for each of the published measures are available for the recent period (up to the last four weeks). Longer historic data records may be available separately. Each reading comprises a reference to the measure being read (identified by its URI), a date time stamp for when the reading applies and a numeric value. The set of readings is updated every 15 minutes, but the individual measures may be updated less frequently than this.</p>

<h3>API</h3>

<p>To list all readings (not very useful without filtering):</p>
<div class="indented"><a href="/flood-monitoring/data/readings?_limit=100">https://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/data/readings</a></div>

<p>To list all readings for a particular measure:<p>
<div class="indented"><a href="/flood-monitoring/id/measures/1491TH-level-stage-i-15_min-mASD/readings?_sorted&_limit=100">https://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/id/measures/{id}/readings</a></div>

<p>To list all readings from a particular station:<p>
<div class="indented"><a href="/flood-monitoring/id/stations/1491TH/readings?_sorted&_limit=100">https://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/id/stations/{id}/readings</a></div>

<p>Note: The base segment for readings is <code>data</code> whereas for identifiable <em>things</em> (stations, measures, flood areas) it is <code>id</code>. This is deliberate and based on URI pattern advice from UK goverment, and UKGovLD working groups <a href="https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/designing-uri-sets-for-the-uk-public-sector" title="This link takes you to a third party site" aria-label="Designing URI sets for the UK public sector - This link takes you to a third party site">[1]</a><a href="https://github.com/UKGovLD/URI-patterns-core/blob/master/URI%20Patterns.md" title="This link takes you to a third party site" aria-label="URI Patterns - This link takes you to a third party site">[2]</a>. </p>

<p>The set of readings can be filtered by time period and by type of measurement.</p>

<p>Filters for time period:</p>
   <table class="table table-condensed table-bordered">
        <thead>
            <tr><th>Query</th><th>Meaning</th></tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
            <tr><td><code class="nowrap">?latest</code></td><td>Return only the most recently available reading for each included measure.</td></tr>
            <tr><td><code class="nowrap">?today</code></td><td>Return all the readings taken today for each included measure.</td></tr>
            <tr><td><code class="nowrap">?date=2015-02-05</code></td><td>Return all the readings taken on the specified day for each included measure.</td></tr>
            <tr><td><code class="nowrap">?startdate=2015-02-05&amp;enddate=2015-02-07</code></td><td>Return the readings taken on the specified range of days for each included measure, up to the specified <code>_limit</code>. If no <code>_limit</code> is given see the following <a href="#size-limits">size limits</a> section.</td></tr>
        </tbody>
    </table>

<p>Filters for time period, available for readings for a particular measure or station only:</p>
    <table class="table table-condensed table-bordered">
        <thead>
            <tr><th>Query</th><th>Meaning</th></tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
            <tr><td><code class="nowrap">?since=2016-09-07T10:30:00Z</code></td><td>Return the readings taken since the given date time (not inclusive), up to the specified <code>_limit</code>. If no <code>_limit</code> is given see the following <a href="#size-limits">size limits</a> section. Typically when tracking a particular measurement then use the dateTime of the last retrieved value as the <code>since</code> parameter to find any new readings. Will accept a simple date value such as <code>2016-09-07</code> which will be interpreted as <code>2016-09-07T:00:00:00Z</code>.</td></tr>
        </tbody>
    </table>

<p>Filters for measurement to include:</p>
   <table class="table table-condensed table-bordered">
        <thead>
            <tr><th>Query</th><th>Meaning</th></tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
            <tr><td><code class="nowrap">?parameter=x</code></td><td>Return only readings for measures of parameters with the given short form name <code>x</code>, for example <em>level</em> or <em>flow</em>.</td></tr>
            <tr><td><code class="nowrap">?qualifier=x</code></td><td>Return only readings of measures with qualifier <code>x</code>. Useful qualifiers are <em>Stage</em> and <em>Downstream Stage</em> (for stations such as weirs which measure levels at two locations), <em>Groundwater</em> for groundwater levels as opposed to river levels and <em>Tidal Level</em> for tidal levels.</td></tr>
            <tr><td><code class="nowrap">?stationReference=x</code></td><td>Return only readings of measures which are available from the station with the reference identifier <code>x</code>.</td></tr>
            <tr><td><code class="nowrap">?station=x</code></td><td>Return only readings of measures which are available from the station with the URI <code>x</code>.</td></tr>
        </tbody>
    </table>

<p>Other modifiers:</p>
   <table class="table table-condensed table-bordered">
        <thead>
            <tr><th>Query</th><th>Meaning</th></tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
            <tr><td><code class="nowrap">?_view=full</code></td><td>Return an inline description of the measure to which the reading applies.</td></tr>
            <tr><td><code class="nowrap">?_sorted</code></td><td>Order the array of returned readings into descending order by date, this done before the limits is applied thus enabling you to fetch the most recent n readings.</td></tr>
        </tbody>
    </table>

<h3>Examples</h3>

<p>Return the latest value for all measurements in CSV format:</p>
<div class="indented"><a href="/flood-monitoring/data/readings.csv?latest&_limit=6000">https://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/data/readings.csv?latest&amp;_limit=6000</a></div>

<p>Return the latest readings from all groundwater measurements:</p>
<div class="indented"><a href="/flood-monitoring/data/readings?latest&qualifier=Groundwater">https://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/data/readings?latest&amp;qualifier=Groundwater</a></div>

<p>Return the latest flow readings:</p>
<div class="indented"><a href="/flood-monitoring/data/readings?latest&parameter=flow">https://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/data/readings?latest&amp;parameter=flow</a></div>
<p>Return the latest flow readings, with descriptions of the measurements:</p>
<div class="indented"><a href="/flood-monitoring/data/readings?latest&parameter=flow&_view=full">https://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/data/readings?latest&amp;parameter=flow&amp;_view=full</a></div>

<p>Return the most recent 10 readings from the upstream level measurement at King's Mill on the River Cherwell:</p>
<div class="indented"><a href="/flood-monitoring/id/measures/1491TH-level-stage-i-15_min-mASD/readings?_sorted&_limit=10">https://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/id/measures/1491TH-level-stage-i-15_min-mASD/readings?_sorted&amp;_limit=10</a></div>

<h3 id="size-limits">Size limits</h3>

<p>By default the readings API endpoints have a limit of 500 items, this can be modified by providing an explicit <code>_limit</code> value up to a hard limit of 10000 items.</p>
<p>This default can be modified depending on the query parameters used. The following table shows the parameters that affect the default, ordered from most important to least.</p>

<table class="table table-condensed table-bordered">
    <thead>
    <tr>
        <th>Parameter</th>
        <th>Default limit</th>
    </tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
    <tr>
        <td><code>measure</code></td>
        <td>none</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td><code>_sorted</code></td>
        <td>500</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td><code>date</code></td>
        <td>none</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td><code>today</code></td>
        <td>none</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td><code>latest</code></td>
        <td>none</td>
    </tr>
    </tbody>
</table>

<p>This means that if a query includes the <code>date</code> parameter, but neither the <code>measure</code> parameter or the <code>_sorted</code> parameter then there is no default limit.</p>
<p>Similarly, if a query includes the <code>_sorted</code> parameter, but not the <code>measure</code> parameter then the default is 500.</p>

<h3>Returned data</h3>
<table class='table table-condensed table-bordered'>
  <thead>
    <tr><th>Field</th><th>Meaning</th><th>Type</th><th>Occurs</th></tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td><code>date</code></td><td>The date at which the reading occurred</td><td>xsd:date</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>dateTime</code></td><td>The date time at which the reading occurred</td><td>xsd:dateTime</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>measure</code></td><td>The URI of the measure being recorded in this reading, this define the location (station), the parameter being measured and other qualifying information.</td><td>rt:Measure</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>value</code></td><td>The value of the reading for the associated measurement, a double not a decimal since some values are NaN. Note that in JSON output NaN is illegal for a number so in JSON any NaN readings will omit the rt:value.</td><td>xsd:double</td><td></td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
<p>Structure of nested field <code>measure</code>:</p><table class='table table-condensed table-bordered'>
  <thead>
    <tr><th>Field</th><th>Meaning</th><th>Type</th><th>Occurs</th></tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td><code>datumType</code></td><td>For level measurements this indicates the type of reference point the level is measured from. Can be relative to the Ordnance Survey datum (rt:AOD), to a local stage datum (rt:ASD) or rt:BDAT (below datum?).</td><td></td><td>optional</td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>parameter</code></td><td>Short, cannonical, name of the quantity being measured e.g. "level", "flow" or "temperature".</td><td>string</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>period</code></td><td>The period between successive readings, in seconds.</td><td>xsd:decimal</td><td>optional</td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>qualifier</code></td><td>A qualilfier for the quantity being measured. Most common use is to separate level measures which occur at the top ("Stage") or bottom ("Downstream Stage") of a sluice or weir. Other relevant qualifiers are "Tidal Level" and "Groundwater".</td><td>string</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>station</code></td><td>The URI of the monitoring station supplying the measure</td><td>rdfs:Resource</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>stationReference</code></td><td>Identifier for the telemetry feed used by the Environment Agency's National Flood Forecasting System</td><td>string</td><td></td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>unitName</code></td><td>A  name for the units for this measurement including the datumType. Typical values are mAOD (for metres relative to the Ordnance Survey datum), mASD (for metres relative to the local stage datum), m (for metres with an unspecified datum) and m3/s (for flow rates).</td><td>xsd:string</td><td>optional</td></tr>
    <tr><td><code>valueType</code></td><td>Indicates whether the measured value is an instantaneous reading or a total, mean or maximum over the period.</td><td></td><td>optional</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
<p>Structure of nested field <code>station</code>:</p><table class='table table-condensed table-bordered'>
  <thead>
    <tr><th>Field</th><th>Meaning</th><th>Type</th><th>Occurs</th></tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td><code>label</code></td><td>A name for the item</td><td>xsd:string</td><td></td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

<p>By default the response will not include the date (just the datetime) nor the expanded description of the measure unless an explicit <code>_view=full</code> request is made.</p>

<span class="anchor" id="historic-readings"></span>
<h2>Historic Readings</h2>

<p>The measurement readings are archived daily as dump files in CSV format. Both the short form and the <code>_view=full</code> form are available.</p>

<p>The data is available from <a href="/flood-monitoring/archive">https://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/archive</a> with individual archives being at <span class="linkColour">https://environment.data.gov.uk/flood-monitoring/archive/readings-{full-}{date}.csv</span>.</p>

<span class="anchor" id="5dfx"></span>
<h2>Five-day flood risk forecast</h2>

<p>The flood risk forecast is produced by the Flood Forecasting Centre (FFC) on a daily basis.
It is issued more frequently when serious flooding is forecast. It provides the indication of the potential for flooding for five days: the day on which it is issued and the subsequent four days ahead.</p>
<p>
The forecast highlights flood risk on a county by county basis and includes a short
commentary on the situation. It covers flooding from rivers, the sea, surface water
and groundwater for England and Wales.</p>

<h3>API</h3>

<p>For documentation on the five-day flood forecast API, see <a href="https://api.foursources.metoffice.gov.uk/docs/flood-guidance-statement-api-public"  title="This link takes you to a third party site" aria-label="Documentation on the five-day flood forecast API - This link takes you to a third party site">https://api.foursources.metoffice.gov.uk/docs/flood-guidance-statement-api-public</a>.</p>

    <div class='definition'>Name of river associated with this monitoring station (when available)</div>
    <div class='term' id='definition-riverOrSea'>riverOrSea (rt:riverOrSea)</div>
    <div class='definition'>Name of the river or sea area linked to the flood area</div>
    <div class='term' id='definition-scaleMax'>scaleMax (rt:scaleMax)</div>
    <div class='definition'>The maximum of the scale suitable for displaying this measurement.</div>
    <div class='term' id='definition-severity'>severity (rt:severity)</div>
    <div class='definition'>The severity of the warning as a text label: 'Flood Alert', 'Flood Warning', 'Severe Flood Warning' or 'Warning no Longer in Force'</div>
    <div class='term' id='definition-severityLevel'>severityLevel (rt:severityLevel)</div>
    <div class='definition'>Severity level code:  1 = 'Severe Flood Warning', 2 = 'Flood Warning', 3 = 'Flood Alert', 4 = 'Warning no Longer in Force'</div>
    <div class='term' id='definition-stageScale'>stageScale (rt:stageScale)</div>
    <div class='definition'>Scale limits and historic range for the main stage water level measure</div>
    <div class='term' id='definition-station'>station (rt:station)</div>
    <div class='definition'>The URI of the monitoring station supplying the measure</div>
    <div class='term' id='definition-stationReference'>stationReference (rt:stationReference)</div>
    <div class='definition'>Identifier for the telemetry feed used by the Environment Agency's National Flood Forecasting System</div>
    <div class='term' id='definition-timeMessageChanged'>timeMessageChanged (rt:timeMessageChanged)</div>
    <div class='definition'>The date and time when the message was last changed</div>
    <div class='term' id='definition-timeRaised'>timeRaised (rt:timeRaised)</div>
    <div class='definition'>The date and time the warning was first raised</div>
    <div class='term' id='definition-timeSeverityChanged'>timeSeverityChanged (rt:timeSeverityChanged)</div>
    <div class='definition'>The date and time when the severity level was last changed</div>
    <div class='term' id='definition-total'>total (rt:total)</div>
    <div class='definition'>Measurements which represent an accumulated total over the measurement period.</div>
    <div class='term' id='definition-town'>town (rt:town)</div>
    <div class='definition'>Name of the nearest town (or named place) to the station</div>
    <div class='term' id='definition-type'>type (rdf:type)</div>
    <div class='definition'>The class, or classes, of this item</div>
    <div class='term' id='definition-typicalRangeHigh'>typicalRangeHigh (rt:typicalRangeHigh)</div>
    <div class='definition'>The top of the typical range band - the measurement exceeded this for 5% of the relevant data on record</div>
    <div class='term' id='definition-typicalRangeLow'>typicalRangeLow (rt:typicalRangeLow)</div>
    <div class='definition'>The bottom of the typical range band - the measurement exceeded this for 95% of the relevant data on record</div>
    <div class='term' id='definition-unit'>unit (rt:unit)</div>
    <div class='definition'>The units in which this parameter is measured, e.g. qudt:Meter</div>
    <div class='term' id='definition-unitName'>unitName (rt:unitName)</div>
    <div class='definition'>A  name for the units for this measurement including the datumType. Typical values are mAOD (for metres relative to the Ordnance Survey datum), mASD (for metres relative to the local stage datum), m (for metres with an unspecified datum) and m3/s (for flow rates).</div>
    <div class='term' id='definition-value'>value (rt:value)</div>
    <div class='definition'>The value of the reading for the associated measurement, a double not a decimal since some values are NaN. Note that in JSON output NaN is illegal for a number so in JSON any NaN readings will omit the rt:value.</div>
    <div class='term' id='definition-valueType'>valueType (rt:valueType)</div>
    <div class='definition'>Indicates whether the measured value is an instantaneous reading or a total, mean or maximum over the period.</div>
    <div class='term' id='definition-wiskiID'>wiskiID (rt:wiskiID)</div>
    <div class='definition'>Identifier for the station in the WISKI hydrology dataset</div>
</div>

    </div>
</div>

<script>
    var navButton = document.querySelector('#navButton');
    var navMenu = document.querySelector('#navMenu');

    navButton.addEventListener('click', function () {
        if (navMenu.classList.contains('is-active')) {
            this.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
            navMenu.classList.remove('is-active');
            navMenu.setAttribute('aria-hidden', 'true');
        } else {
            navMenu.classList.add('is-active');
            this.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
            navMenu.setAttribute('aria-hidden', 'false');
        }
    });
</script>
